skill.name: neovim-debugging
skill.description: Debug Neovim and LazyVim configuration problems with structured diagnosis, headless Neovim checks, plugin loading analysis, and targeted user questions.
skill.summary: Diagnose Neovim and LazyVim configuration failures with focused evidence gathering and step-by-step fixes.
skill.author: BitYoungjae

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown examples, Neovim keymap terminology, and local diagnostic command snippets. I found no prompt-injection attempt or exfiltration intent. The skill encourages programmatic local inspection before asking the user, which creates a moderate privacy and consent risk.

remediation.suggestion: Ask for user approval before reading hidden home configuration files or running headless commands, and state the exact path and purpose.
Replace broad cat, grep, and glob examples with targeted reads and guidance to redact tokens, private paths, and credentials.
Tell agents to review substitutions before running commands that include module names, plugin names, or user-provided paths.

content.value_statement: Neovim configuration failures can be hard to isolate across plugins, keymaps, and startup state. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused diagnostics, local checks, and clear fixes.
actual_capabilities: Classifies issues as Lua errors, keymap failures, plugin loading problems, performance issues, UI problems, or LSP failures.
Provides headless Neovim checks for options, mappings, plugin state, and configuration values.
Maps common Lua, module, Vim API, and plugin errors to likely causes and fixes.
Guides LazyVim and plugin diagnostics for lazy.nvim, which-key, LSP, Telescope, nvim-cmp, Treesitter, and Snacks.nvim.
Helps ask narrow user questions when automated checks cannot confirm visual or interactive behavior.
limitations: Requires Neovim and relevant plugins to be installed in the user environment.
Command examples may need user approval and should be reviewed before running.
Does not replace upstream plugin documentation for every plugin version.
Cannot verify visual UI behavior without user feedback or screenshots.

use_cases.title: Fix Broken Keymaps
use_cases.description: Trace missing or shadowed mappings through leader settings, which-key behavior, and plugin load state.

use_cases.title: Investigate Plugin Loading
use_cases.description: Check whether lazy-loaded plugins are declared, installed, loaded, and configured at the right time.

use_cases.title: Triage Lua Startup Errors
use_cases.description: Decode Lua stack traces, identify the failing module, and separate user config issues from plugin issues.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Keymap
prompt_templates.prompt: My Neovim keymap does not work. Use the neovim-debugging workflow to identify likely causes and tell me the smallest evidence you need.

prompt_templates.title: Check Plugin Loading
prompt_templates.prompt: A LazyVim plugin is installed but its feature is missing. Diagnose whether the plugin is declared, loaded, configured, or blocked by lazy loading.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Lua Error
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a Neovim Lua error with a stack trace. Analyze the failure path, identify the likely owner, and propose a focused fix plan.

prompt_templates.title: Profile Slow Startup
prompt_templates.prompt: My Neovim startup is slow after recent plugin changes. Build a diagnostic plan that compares baseline, minimal config, and slow startup entries.

output_examples.input: My localleader mappings do not appear in which-key.
output_examples.output: Diagnosis focuses on whether which-key loads, whether localleader is set before mappings, and whether localleader triggers are configured. The likely fix is adding a localleader trigger or registering descriptions correctly.

output_examples.input: Telescope stopped working after updating plugins.
output_examples.output: The workflow compares lazy-lock changes, checks whether Telescope and its extensions load, and separates API changes from configuration mistakes.

output_examples.input: Neovim startup became slow this week.
output_examples.output: The skill measures startup time, identifies slow require or sourcing entries, compares minimal config behavior, and narrows the problem to recent plugin or config changes.

best_practices: Start with the exact symptom and one likely hypothesis before running diagnostics.
Ask for approval before broad file inspection or long-running commands.
Test one change at a time and confirm the symptom is fixed.
anti_patterns: Running every diagnostic command before understanding the symptom.
Reading entire configuration trees when targeted checks are enough.
Assuming a plugin bug before checking load state, version, and configuration.

faq.question: Does this skill run Neovim commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides command examples for local diagnosis. Users or agents should review commands before running them.

faq.question: Can it debug LazyVim-specific problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes LazyVim structure, extras, lazy.nvim loading, and common override patterns.

faq.question: Does it support plugin-specific troubleshooting?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers lazy.nvim, which-key, LSP, Treesitter, Telescope, nvim-cmp, and Snacks.nvim patterns.

faq.question: Can it fix every Neovim plugin issue?
faq.answer: No. It helps isolate causes, but plugin-specific breaking changes may require upstream documentation or issue trackers.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the exact symptom, any error message, the action that triggers it, and whether it started after a change.

faq.question: Is it useful for performance problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes startup timing, minimal configuration comparison, and runtime profiling guidance.
